item.title: You Can See Everything, 2026 - ★★★★★
item.description: At a Halloween party this weekend, a guy I'd never seen walked in, interrupted our conversation without introducing himself and said "all I want to talk about right now is You Can See Everything. Have any of you seen it?" The monoculture is back baby! And instead of your usual Real Housewives, Tiger Kings, or other Insane Person of the Week watercooler topics, there's actually something to talk about, more nuance than "this crazy person desperately wants attention". Or maybe not, and all the narratives are made up, everyone involved is still just seeking attention in their own ways, and there's as much artifice here as reality TV. But there's also full frontal, so that's kind of nice to talk about too.

item.title: Digger, 2026 - ★★★ (contains spoilers)
item.description:
This review may contain spoilers.

Starts pretty obnoxious and unfunny and then it peels back a layer and goes "gotcha! We know these jokes are hack. We're being annoying on PURPOSE" and it's a bit of a relief. Then it puts the layer back on and you think "wait, didn't you just tell me this sucks?" And then Cruise gives his UN monologue and you think "oh maybe this play actually IS interesting" and then the movie doubles down and smugly says "nope, it sucks. Got ya again!" but still forces you to watch the rest of it - often beautifully handmade and technically crafted, but always self-satisfied and obnoxious. In any case, I surprisingly found myself enjoying going on this little annoying journey, and Tom Cruise wears a big hat, and I think we can all agree that that's worth $200 million.

item.description: I never really liked the Roadrunner cartoons because it always stressed me out how much would go wrong for Wile E Coyote so it's sort of embarrassing how cathartic and moving this was for me. But even more embarrassing is that I didn't realize that the annual carrot festival would tie into the plot or Bugs Bunny. I'm a dumb guy and thought it was just a bit on how boring Albuquerque is. There's a lot I love here, but maybe I'm an easy mark because Who Framed Roger Rabbit is one of my all time favorites and just hearing "carrot festival" is honestly still kind of funny to me.

item.title: Wayne's World, 1992
item.description: In one of my most spontaneous moviegoing nights to date, after dinner and drinks on our last night vacationing in Chicago, gf and I happened to walk by an indie theater with Wayne's World on the marquee. We walked in, found out it started in 5 minutes, and got tickets. A perfectly dumb and joyous Chicago-based movie to endcap our trip. Unfortunately I can't rate this viewing properly as the drinks caught up to me and I had spend about 15 minutes in the bathroom doing breathing exercises so I didn't vomit (hurl, spew, etc), but it's still nice to be whimsical every once in a while.
